Synopsis:
    European gasoline refinery margins hit near-record levels (~$62.07/bbl premium to Brent), approaching the June 2022 all-time high of $62.10/bbl. The tightening is driven by refinery attacks in the Middle East and Russia reducing refined fuel supply, compounded by low Rhine water levels in NW Europe hampering barge logistics into the ARA hub. The article is a spot market observation with no explicit forward guidance.

Q01. Is the content's main message about EU energy, EU commodities, German power market prices, German energy economics?
Relevance: YES (EU energy & commodities — specifically European gasoline refinery margins and ARA hub logistics; not directly about German power markets or economics)

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 35 (Middle East/Ukraine supply disruption risks are well-established narratives; low Rhine levels affecting ARA is a recurring seasonal pattern. The near-record margin level adds a new data point but the underlying drivers are broadly known)
